key_insight: Physics-informed circuits, compact gauge-field encodings, and operator truncation advance digital quantum simulation of interacting-field dynamics.
engineering_relevance: These methods reduce qubit and circuit-depth demands for quantum simulations targeting real-time QCD phenomena such as energy loss and hadronization.
method: Prepare interacting ground states and evolve a heavy quark through light quarks in 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory.
Digitize a fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis using as few as three qubits per plaquette.
Apply Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) during adiabatic preparation of a λφ⁴ ground state.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware validation against classical benchmarks, low-energy observables reproduced to 10⁻³ precision with compact digitization, and approximately 30% circuit-depth reduction using SeqHT.
watch_item: Resource overhead still limits scaling, and truncations must preserve the observables relevant to each target system.
paper_title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
